          Manchester United’s WSL Turnaround: Is the Eva Olid Effect Taking Shape?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 28, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After a difficult start, Manchester United are beginning to show what Eva Olid wants them to be. Now fourth in the WSL table, the signs of progress are encouraging, but are United really turning a corner?
Criticism can fall quickly on new managers, and the football industry has a habit of judging a seed before it has had time to take root.
Cast your mind back four matchdays and you might recall a forlorn figure on the touchline, seemingly wrestling with the task of turning her vision into reality.
Eva Olid has faced her share of scrutiny since taking charge at Manchester United, including from us just last month.

Questions centred on the defensive frailties exposed in United’s opening two games against London City Lionesses and Chelsea, especially the 5-0 thrashing against the Blues, while Olid’s vision for a possession-based, attack-minded side was difficult to discern.
Their opening two defeats made it just the second time in WSL history that United had started a season with back-to-back losses, following their debut campaign in 2019-20.
Fast-forward to now and the picture could not look more different.

United are unbeaten in their last six games in all competitions, with their 1-1 draw against Manchester City last time out offering the clearest sign yet that Olid’s ideas are taking hold against the league’s best.

They are also outperforming their expected points tally by 4.3 points, the largest margin in the league. But is this just down to good fortune, or do the underlying numbers point to genuine improvement?
The draw against City was not simply a case of the Red Devils hanging on for a point against their neighbours, but it was a performance backed by belief that three points were there for the taking.
Andrée Jeglertz’s side completed a WSL double over United last season, winning both games 3-0. This time, the contest was far more evenly matched.

As you can see from the respective zones of control below, in this fixture last season, City controlled the majority of zones on the pitch. However, United had more control in their own half this time around, and imposed themselves on the game far more.
Though United started on the front foot, City grew into the contest and the hosts were forced to absorb pressure. Unlike in their heavy defeat to Chelsea, though, they found ways to push back.

United’s 45.6% field tilt – a metric that measures territorial dominance by looking at the share of possession each side has in their attacking third compared to their opponent – was their highest against one of the WSL’s traditional top three since recording 50% against Chelsea in April 2025. Against City, it was their best figure since May 2023, when they registered 56.4%.
They also recorded 13 high turnovers, their third-most against the traditional top three in WSL history.
Their average of 3.62 passes per sequence against City was also their third-highest against any traditional top three opponent in the WSL.

Add those all together and the figures suggest a side no longer content to sit back. United were competing for the ball higher up the pitch, sustaining possession and looking to exploit City’s defensive weaknesses.
Their best passages came when they moved the ball quickly. One- and two-touch combinations offered a glimpse of Olid’s philosophy at its most effective, even against the reigning champions.
The clearest example came when Ella Toone backheeled the ball into Andrea Medina’s path, helping to create an opening for Julia Zigiotti Olme.
After the game, Olid said: “If we play like this, nothing can stop us.”
